slides.1.highlights.0.title: AOG and AOC
slides.1.highlights.0.content: AOG: at least 12° natural, no enrichment, no irrigation in principle, yields set yearly. AOC: inside an AOG, with its own rules and irrigation up to a deadline
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Guerrouane and Beni-M'Tir
slides.1.highlights.1.content: West and east of the Meknès–El Hajeb road, with the AOC Coteaux de l'Atlas on the east
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Coteaux de l'Atlas and Côtes de Rommani
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Both cap yields at 60 hl/ha; Rommani is half a degree higher and requires hand-picking and trellising
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Rules and reality
slides.1.highlights.3.content: The AOC rules favour international grapes while national plantings stay traditional, and places outside the AOGs such as Essaouira also make good wine
slides.1.content: If you can explain each comparison, you have mastered this course.
slides.2.componentProps.slide.title: 📋 Final assessment
How many AOGs does Morocco have according to ONSSA?
Five is the teaching zones, and three is the AOCs on the ONSSA page.
Which AOG contains the AOC Les Coteaux de l'Atlas?
What is the yield limit for Les Coteaux de l'Atlas?
It may be adjusted yearly according to the harvest.
Which group must be at least two-thirds of red Coteaux de l'Atlas?
A. Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah, Tempranillo
Which equipment do the general AOC rules ban?
B. Continuous presses and screw conveyors
Order 1955-98, article 3; stainless steel and cooling are actually required.
May an AOC wine not classified by the national commission use "1er cru"?
B. Yes, after five years' ageing
It needs an AOC terroir, traditionally affirmed quality and classification by the commission.
May a Moroccan label say "Vin de pays"?
D. No, the rules explicitly ban it
Short answer: compare the main differences between Moroccan AOG and AOC.
An AOC must lie within an AOG
AOG needs 12° natural with no enrichment; AOC may be allowed enrichment in very poor years
AOG yields are set yearly; AOCs such as Coteaux de l'Atlas have a 60 hl/ha limit
AOG is not irrigated in principle; AOC may irrigate until set dates

An AOC sits within an AOG and has its own grape, sugar, yield and planting rules. An AOG requires at least 12° natural alcohol with no enrichment and, in principle, no irrigation, with yields set each year. An AOC has set limits, allows irrigation up to a date and may be allowed enrichment in very poor years.
Short answer: why was Moroccan output high in the 1950s yet at a low point by the early 1990s?
Large-scale planting for export under the French
EEC quotas from 1967 shrank the export market
State control and fixed grape prices removed incentives for quality

The French-era vineyards were planted mainly for export. After independence, the 1967 quotas shrank the market, then state control and fixed prices removed any incentive for quality, and the vines aged, leaving a low point by the early 1990s.
